title: Brier score decomposition and expected calibration error
purpose: Split the Brier score of probability forecasts into reliability, resolution, uncertainty and the two within-bin terms that make the decomposition exact for binned forecasts, and compute the expected calibration error. Use it to tell miscalibration apart from lack of discrimination.

entry_points.name: brier_decomposition
entry_points.arguments: forecasts in [0, 1]; outcomes 0 or 1; bins (equal width, default 10)
entry_points.returns: {brier, reliability, resolution, uncertainty, within_bin_variance, within_bin_covariance, identity_residual, bins}

assumptions: Outcomes are binary and forecasts are probabilities of outcome 1.
Bins are equal width on [0, 1]; a forecast of exactly 1 joins the last bin.
guarantees: brier = reliability - resolution + uncertainty + within_bin_variance - within_bin_covariance up to rounding; identity_residual reports the difference.
With identical forecasts inside each bin the two within-bin terms are 0 and the three-term Murphy decomposition is recovered.
ECE is the count-weighted mean absolute gap between bin mean forecast and bin outcome rate.

known_wrong.name: three_terms_are_not_the_score
known_wrong.why: REL - RES + UNC equals the Brier score only when forecasts inside a bin are identical; here it overstates it by 0.0133.

limits: Equal-width bins only; reliability, resolution and ECE all depend on the binning, and ECE is biased upward for small bins. Binary outcomes only. No confidence intervals are computed.
technique_references: A new vector partition of the probability score (Murphy)
Two extra components in the Brier score decomposition (Stephenson, Coelho and Jolliffe)
Expected calibration error (Naeini, Cooper and Hauskrecht)
